boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten documented campus spaces for collaborative work, quiet study, gathering, and recreation.

cards.title: Set up in the Research Commons
cards.subtitle: Hesburgh Library, first floor
cards.notes: Use the northeast-corner tables or lounge chairs when you want daylight and a setting where individual and collaborative work are both supported.
cards.short_summary: A window-lined first-floor library area built for solo or collaborative work.
cards.evidence_claim: Hesburgh Libraries identifies the Research Commons as a first-floor space with tables and lounge chairs for individual and collaborative work.
cards.access_notes: Located on the first floor, northeast corner, just off the North Entrance.

cards.title: Work around the Collaboration Hub
cards.subtitle: Hesburgh Library, first floor
cards.notes: Bring a small group to the northwest corner for tables, study nooks, mobile monitors, whiteboards, and nearby group or videoconference rooms.
cards.short_summary: A flexible library hub with shared work surfaces and collaboration tools.
cards.evidence_claim: Hesburgh Libraries lists tables, study nooks, group rooms, videoconference rooms, mobile monitors, and whiteboards in the Collaboration Hub.
cards.access_notes: Located on the first floor northwest corner, just off the North Entrance.

cards.title: Take a table in Scholars Lounge
cards.subtitle: Hesburgh Library concourse
cards.notes: Choose a large table for a collaborative session, or use the smaller tables and lounge seating for a quieter individual study break.
cards.short_summary: A concourse lounge that supports both table work and casual conversation.
cards.evidence_claim: Hesburgh Libraries says Mahaffey Scholars Lounge offers large collaborative tables, individual tables, couches, and lounge chairs.
cards.access_notes: Located in the Hesburgh Library concourse across from Au Bon Pain.

cards.title: Choose the lower level for quiet work
cards.subtitle: Hesburgh Library, lower level
cards.notes: Use the booths, tables, or lounge chairs when you need focused reading or individual work; the library describes this area as typically low-noise.
cards.short_summary: A lower-level seating area intended for focused, individual study.
cards.evidence_claim: Hesburgh Libraries describes Lower Level Study Seats as low-noise space with booths, tables, lounge chairs, and quiet-study use.
cards.access_notes: Use the Hesburgh Library lower-level floor map for the current location and layout.

cards.title: Book a first-floor group room
cards.subtitle: Hesburgh Library Collaboration Hub
cards.notes: Reserve a room for two or more people when you need a whiteboard and focused group space; unreserved non-multimedia rooms are first-come, first-served.
cards.short_summary: Reservable Collaboration Hub rooms for small-group work.
cards.evidence_claim: Hesburgh Libraries states its group study rooms are reservable for collaborative work and, when unreserved, generally first-come, first-served.
cards.source_title: Group Study Rooms Reservation Policy | Hesburgh Libraries
cards.access_notes: First-floor rooms are in the northwest corner of the Collaboration Hub; reservations have participation and time-limit requirements.

cards.title: Meet beneath the library mural
cards.subtitle: Outside Hesburgh Library
cards.notes: Use the outdoor benches, bistro tables, and chairs beneath Word of Life for an informal meeting or alternative study session near library collections.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor library courtyard with seating for studying and meeting.
cards.evidence_claim: Hesburgh Libraries describes Carey Courtyard as an outdoor seating area that became an alternative study and meeting space.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor space at the Hesburgh Library entrance; use weather-appropriate judgment.

cards.title: Use LaFortune as a campus base
cards.subtitle: Central campus student center
cards.notes: Stop in to meet, eat, study, or connect with student organizations; Student Activities identifies LaFortune among its campus spaces for these uses.
cards.short_summary: A central student center with organizational and administrative offices.
cards.evidence_claim: Notre Dame Student Activities says LaFortune Student Center offers space to gather, eat, perform, meet, and study.
cards.source_title: Student Activities Office | University of Notre Dame
cards.access_notes: LaFortune also houses departmental, organizational, and administrative offices; follow current building access rules.

cards.entity_name: Jan and Marty Hiller Midfield Commons
cards.title: Gather in Midfield Commons
cards.subtitle: Duncan Student Center, first and second floors
cards.notes: Use the commons’ open seating for presentations, game watches, or non-ticketed events; it remains designated public space during daily building operations.
cards.short_summary: A multi-level Duncan gathering space with seating and a large video display.
cards.evidence_claim: Notre Dame lists Midfield Commons for presentations, game watches, and non-ticketed events and designates it as public space.
cards.source_title: Meeting Rooms and Event Spaces | Duncan Student Center
cards.access_notes: Reservations and activities are limited so they do not interfere with daily operations; access is subject to building policies.

cards.title: Use the Graduate Student Lounge
cards.subtitle: Duncan Student Center, second floor
cards.notes: Graduate and professional students can meet, eat, study, rest, or relax among varied seating; reserve its small conference room for focused group work.
cards.short_summary: A second-floor graduate and professional student lounge with work and break amenities.
cards.evidence_claim: Notre Dame Graduate Student Life describes the Graduate Student Lounge as space for graduate and professional students to meet, eat, study, rest, and relax.
cards.source_title: Grad Lounge in Duncan Student Center | University of Notre Dame
cards.access_notes: On the south side of Duncan’s second floor; the lounge is open when Duncan Student Center is open, and the conference room may be reserved.

cards.title: Move with a group at Rockne
cards.subtitle: South Quad, Dorr Road and Holy Cross Drive
cards.notes: Plan a recreation visit for club sports, intramurals, fitness classes, aquatic instruction, or general recreation after confirming facility hours and eligibility.
cards.short_summary: A South Quad recreation facility with pools, courts, fitness equipment, and club programming.
cards.evidence_claim: Notre Dame RecSports identifies Rockne Memorial as a site for club sports, intramurals, fitness classes, aquatic instruction, and general recreation.
cards.source_title: Rockne Memorial | RecSports | University of Notre Dame
cards.access_notes: RecSports access requires a valid Notre Dame ID for students, faculty, staff, and retirees; confirm current operating hours before visiting.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten no-admission ways to spend time around Notre Dame’s public art, campus, library, and sacred spaces.

cards.title: Browse the Raclin Murphy galleries
cards.subtitle: Notre Dame Arts Gateway
cards.notes: Meet by the east entrance, choose a gallery floor, and trade observations on a few works before looping back through the public spaces.
cards.short_summary: A self-paced art outing inside Notre Dame’s public museum.
cards.evidence_claim: The Raclin Murphy Museum of Art is always free and open to all.
cards.source_title: Visit | Raclin Murphy Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday–Sunday; closed Mondays and major holidays. Check the museum’s current hours before going.

cards.title: Pause in the museum chapel
cards.subtitle: Level 2, Raclin Murphy Museum of Art
cards.notes: Visit quietly with a friend, take in the mosaic and stained glass, then leave time for a low-key conversation outside the chapel.
cards.short_summary: A contemplative chapel surrounded by art galleries.
cards.evidence_claim: The chapel is a visitor space for quiet contemplation and is within the Raclin Murphy Museum, which is always free and open to all.
cards.source_title: Mary, Queen of Families Chapel | Raclin Murphy Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Enter during museum hours; the museum lists free admission for all visitors.

cards.entity_name: International Modern and Contemporary Art Galleries
cards.title: Compare modern and contemporary works
cards.subtitle: Lower Level, Raclin Murphy Museum of Art
cards.notes: Use the four-gallery sequence as a shared prompt: each person picks one work and explains what drew their attention without rushing.
cards.short_summary: Four linked galleries spanning modern and contemporary art.
cards.evidence_claim: The lower-level suite has four galleries exploring modern and contemporary art; the Raclin Murphy Museum is always free and open to all.
cards.source_title: International Modern and Contemporary Art (Lower Level) | Raclin Murphy Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Access is during museum hours; the museum’s visit information states admission is always free.

cards.title: Look up in the Sculpture Court
cards.subtitle: Lower Level, Raclin Murphy Museum of Art
cards.notes: Start at the lower-level sculpture display and take a slow lap together, using the open vertical space to compare scale and materials.
cards.short_summary: A naturally lit, multistory display space for sculpture.
cards.evidence_claim: The Sculpture Court presents sculpture holdings in the museum’s lower-level modern and contemporary galleries; museum admission is always free.
cards.source_title: International Modern and Contemporary Art (Lower Level) | Raclin Murphy Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Visit during museum hours. The museum’s official visit page states it is always free and open to all.

cards.entity_name: Charles B. Hayes Family Sculpture Park
cards.title: Walk the Hayes Sculpture Park
cards.subtitle: Notre Dame Arts Gateway
cards.notes: Follow the paths through the native plantings, stop at a few sculptures, and use the park map to orient your group as you go.
cards.short_summary: A nine-acre outdoor extension of the museum with major sculpture.
cards.evidence_claim: The nine-acre Charles B. Hayes Family Sculpture Park is an outdoor extension of the museum and contains works by multiple major sculptors.
cards.source_title: Hayes Sculpture Park | Raclin Murphy Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: The museum identifies the park as an outdoor extension and lists the museum as always free and open to all.

cards.entity_name: Life of Christ / Cycle of Life
cards.title: Follow the basalt-column artwork
cards.subtitle: Charles B. Hayes Family Sculpture Park
cards.notes: Walk the 42-foot pathway at an unhurried pace, then compare which of the seven episodes each person noticed first.
cards.short_summary: Philip Rickey’s seven-episode public artwork in the sculpture park.
cards.evidence_claim: Philip Rickey’s Life of Christ / Cycle of Life is a public art commission in the Charles B. Hayes Family Sculpture Park, which may be visited year-round.
cards.source_title: Charles B. Hayes Family Sculpture Park guide
cards.access_notes: Outdoor artwork in the sculpture park; the museum’s current visit information states museum access is always free.

cards.title: Take a self-guided Basilica visit
cards.subtitle: 101 Basilica Drive
cards.notes: Enter respectfully, move through the public areas at your own pace, and pause to look closely at the stained glass and chapels.
cards.short_summary: A self-guided visit inside Notre Dame’s Basilica.
cards.evidence_claim: The Basilica welcomes visitors for self-guided tours, is open to the public year-round, and has free admission.
cards.source_title: Visits and Tours | Basilica of the Sacred Heart
cards.access_notes: Hours vary with the academic calendar and special liturgies may close the building; admission is free.

cards.title: See the Basilica Museum
cards.subtitle: West side of the Basilica Sacristy
cards.notes: Check the signage by the Sacristy, then add the museum to a Basilica visit and discuss one sacred-art detail before heading out.
cards.short_summary: A public museum space within the Basilica complex.
cards.evidence_claim: The Basilica Museum is open to the public when indicated by signage, and Basilica admission is free.
cards.source_title: Visits and Tours | Basilica of the Sacred Heart
cards.access_notes: Museum availability varies; confirm the posted sign and note that liturgies or events can close touring areas.

cards.title: Use the visitor-friendly library
cards.subtitle: 284 Hesburgh Library
cards.notes: Meet on the first floor, browse the catalog or use a research workstation, and plan a quiet reading or research session together.
cards.short_summary: Visitor access to library spaces, collections, and research workstations.
cards.evidence_claim: Hesburgh Library is open to visitors, welcomes everyone to use collections on site, and provides research workstations without NetID login.
cards.access_notes: Visitors are asked to leave at 8 p.m., when the building becomes exclusive to current Notre Dame students, faculty, and staff.

cards.title: Join the free public campus tour
cards.subtitle: Starts at Eck Visitors Center
cards.notes: Register in person at the Eck Visitors Center on the day you visit, then use the student-led walk to orient your group to campus landmarks.
cards.short_summary: A free, student-led introduction to signature Notre Dame sites.
cards.evidence_claim: Notre Dame’s public campus tours are free year-round, register in person, and highlight the Golden Dome, Basilica, Grotto, and Word of Life mural.
cards.access_notes: Register in person on the day of your visit at Eck Visitors Center; tour availability may vary.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Notre Dame rituals, residence-hall events, and game-day customs.

cards.title: Wait for the Golden Dome steps
cards.subtitle: Main Building • commencement tradition
cards.notes: Walk past the Main Building steps during your undergraduate years, then notice graduating seniors reclaim them for celebratory photos.
cards.short_summary: Undergraduates traditionally save the front steps for graduation.
cards.evidence_claim: Notre Dame says undergraduates avoid the Main Building steps and traditionally climb them after commencement.
cards.access_notes: Observe public campus access rules and commencement event guidance.

cards.title: Keep off the God Quad grass
cards.subtitle: God Quad • Basilica and Main Building
cards.notes: Cross the paths around God Quad and hear the campus lore: stepping on its grass is said to endanger a theology requirement.
cards.short_summary: A campus superstition protects the grass at Notre Dame’s spiritual center.
cards.evidence_claim: Notre Dame documents the tradition that undergraduates refrain from God Quad grass because of a theology-course legend.
cards.access_notes: Stay on designated walkways and follow posted campus rules.

cards.title: Carry a fleck of the Golden Dome
cards.subtitle: Main Building gold leaf • helmets and diplomas
cards.notes: Look up at the Dome, then connect its regilding to a quieter ritual: leftover leaf is incorporated into helmets and diplomas.
cards.short_summary: Dome gold leaf is reused in two iconic Notre Dame items.
cards.evidence_claim: Notre Dame Admissions states that leftover Golden Dome gold leaf is used in football-helmet paint and graduation diplomas.
cards.access_notes: The Dome is viewable from campus; access to the building follows University rules.

cards.entity_name: South Quad First Snowfall Snowball Fight
cards.title: Mark the first big snowfall on South Quad
cards.subtitle: South Quad • annual winter ritual
cards.notes: When a substantial first snowfall sticks, watch for the campus-wide South Quad snowball fight described by Notre Dame Admissions.
cards.short_summary: The first snow that sticks can cue a campus-wide snowball fight.
cards.evidence_claim: Notre Dame Admissions describes an annual campus-wide snowball fight on South Quad after the first good snowfall.
cards.access_notes: Participate only if conditions and University guidance permit; respect others’ space.

cards.title: Seniors make one last visit to the Grotto
cards.subtitle: Grotto of Our Lady of Lourdes • Senior Week
cards.notes: During Senior Week, seniors gather at the Grotto, light candles, hear from the University president, and reflect before commencement.
cards.short_summary: A candlelit Senior Week gathering marks the transition out of undergraduate life.
cards.evidence_claim: Notre Dame identifies The Last Visit as a Thursday-before-Commencement Grotto tradition for seniors.
cards.access_notes: Scheduled as part of Senior Week; check University commencement information for current details.

cards.title: Hear trumpets fill the Main Building
cards.subtitle: Main Building Rotunda • football Saturdays
cards.notes: On football Saturdays, listen in the Main Building rotunda as the marching band’s trumpet section plays the Alma Mater and Victory March.
cards.short_summary: A short trumpet performance turns the Dome rotunda into a game-day gathering point.
cards.evidence_claim: Notre Dame describes Trumpets Under the Dome as a football-Saturday performance of the Alma Mater and Victory March.
cards.access_notes: Occurs on football Saturdays; confirm game-day programming and building access before visiting.

cards.title: Line the route for the Player Walk
cards.subtitle: Guglielmino Athletics Complex to Notre Dame Stadium
cards.notes: Before home football kickoffs, watch supporters greet the team during its walk from the Gug toward Notre Dame Stadium.
cards.short_summary: The team’s pregame walk is a visible part of the Saturday routine.
cards.evidence_claim: Notre Dame states that fans line up for the Player Walk two hours and 15 minutes before kickoff.
cards.access_notes: Timing depends on the home-football schedule; use crowd-control instructions on game days.

cards.title: Follow the charitable Bengal Bouts
cards.subtitle: Campus boxing series • supports Holy Cross missions
cards.notes: Follow the annual boxing series as a spectator and learn how its Notre Dame tradition directs support toward Holy Cross orphanages and missions.
cards.short_summary: A long-running boxing series ties campus competition to charitable fundraising.
cards.evidence_claim: Notre Dame says Bengal Bouts began in 1931 and raises money for Holy Cross orphanages and missions in Bangladesh.
cards.access_notes: Event dates, venue, and attendance details vary; consult current University event information.

cards.title: Find the festivities of Pop Farley Week
cards.subtitle: Farley Hall • winter residence-hall tradition
cards.notes: Look for Farley Hall’s winter week of events, including Skit Night, a visit to Father John “Pop” Farley’s grave, and seasonal decorations.
cards.short_summary: Farley’s winter tradition honors the hall’s namesake through events and decoration.
cards.evidence_claim: Notre Dame Admissions describes Pop Farley Week as Farley Hall’s annual winter events honoring Father John “Pop” Farley.
cards.source_title: Countdown to Early Action: 6 Stunningly Spectacular Signature Events
cards.access_notes: A residence-hall program; confirm current scheduling and any participation requirements with Farley Hall.

cards.title: Cheer the Ryan Hall wheelchair basketball tournament
cards.subtitle: Ryan Hall signature event • Hammes Bookstore Basketball Courts
cards.notes: Watch or join the traditional five-on-five bracket tournament, a Ryan Hall event that supports Whirlwind Wheelchair International.
cards.short_summary: Ryan Hall pairs a campus tournament with fundraising for sustainable wheelchairs.
cards.evidence_claim: Notre Dame Admissions identifies Ryan Hall’s wheelchair basketball tournament as a traditional fundraiser for Whirlwind Wheelchair International.
cards.source_title: Countdown to Early Action: 6 Stunningly Spectacular Signature Events
cards.access_notes: Confirm the current tournament schedule, registration details, and spectator access with Ryan Hall.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at University of Notre Dame, Shared as Cards
boards.description: An under-21-safe first-weekend route through documented campus landmarks, student spaces, recreation, and the arts.

cards.title: Begin with a campus orientation
cards.subtitle: Eck Visitors Center · Friday afternoon
cards.notes: Check the day’s general-tour times at Eck, then use the historical and social overview to get your bearings before exploring independently.
cards.short_summary: A guided opening that introduces the campus through its signature sites.
cards.evidence_claim: The Eck Visitors Center offers free public general tours, with registration in person beginning 30 minutes before the tour.
cards.source_title: On-Campus Tours | University of Notre Dame
cards.access_notes: Tour dates and times vary; groups of 10 or more must arrange a private tour.

cards.title: Walk up to the Golden Dome
cards.subtitle: Main Building · First landmark loop
cards.notes: Pause outside the Main Building to identify the Golden Dome, then continue on foot toward the Basilica and the Grotto at an unhurried pace.
cards.short_summary: A landmark stop that anchors the first campus walk.
cards.evidence_claim: Notre Dame’s official tours identify the Main Building, known as the Golden Dome, as a regular campus-tour stop.
cards.source_title: On-Campus Tours | University of Notre Dame
cards.access_notes: View from exterior paths; confirm building access locally if planning to enter.

cards.title: Take a self-guided Basilica visit
cards.subtitle: Basilica of the Sacred Heart · Friday afternoon
cards.notes: Enter respectfully for a self-guided look at the church or its museum, and defer to posted closures for liturgies, rehearsals, weddings, or funerals.
cards.short_summary: A quiet architectural and sacred-site visit with a public museum.
cards.evidence_claim: The Basilica is open to the public year-round, welcomes self-guided visits, and states that admission is free.
cards.source_title: Visits and Tours | Basilica of the Sacred Heart
cards.access_notes: Hours vary with the academic calendar; the Basilica and museum may close for services or events.

cards.entity_name: Grotto of Our Lady of Lourdes
cards.title: Make time for the Grotto
cards.subtitle: Grotto · Reflective stop near the Basilica
cards.notes: Use this as a low-key pause: walk through quietly, sit for reflection if appropriate, and leave space for others who are praying.
cards.short_summary: A campus prayer and reflection site used throughout the day and night.
cards.evidence_claim: Notre Dame describes the Grotto as a sacred campus place where students, staff, alumni, and visitors come for quiet reflection and prayer.
cards.access_notes: Treat the site as an active prayer space; no purchase is required to visit.

cards.entity_name: Hesburgh Library and Word of Life mural
cards.title: Find the Word of Life mural
cards.subtitle: Hesburgh Library · Friday evening study reset
cards.notes: Approach the library façade for the mural, then head inside during open visitor hours to locate a study spot or browse the open stacks.
cards.short_summary: A landmark mural paired with the University’s flagship library.
cards.evidence_claim: Notre Dame’s tour materials highlight the Word of Life mural, and Hesburgh Library provides study spaces and general research collections in open stacks.
cards.access_notes: Visitors are asked to leave at 8 p.m., when access becomes exclusive to current students, faculty, and staff.

cards.title: Regroup at LaFortune
cards.subtitle: LaFortune Student Center · Friday evening
cards.notes: Meet your group in the student center, check campus postings, and use the building as a practical reset point before choosing the next activity.
cards.short_summary: A central student-services building for gathering, eating, meetings, and study.
cards.evidence_claim: Notre Dame’s Student Activities Office manages LaFortune Student Center as one of its spaces to gather, eat, perform, meet, and study.
cards.source_title: Student Activities Office | University of Notre Dame
cards.access_notes: Building access and individual food-service availability can change; check current notices on arrival.

cards.title: Schedule a recreational break
cards.subtitle: Rockne Memorial · Saturday daytime
cards.notes: Complete the required recreation waiver before arriving, then choose an available activity rather than assuming every amenity is open on a given day.
cards.short_summary: A historic campus recreation facility with courts, fitness equipment, and pools.
cards.evidence_claim: Rockne Memorial provides recreational facilities including cardio equipment, weight room, pools, racquetball and squash courts, and basketball courts.
cards.source_title: Rockne Memorial | RecSports | University of Notre Dame
cards.access_notes: A RecSports waiver is required; the facility posts seasonal and modified hours, including closures.

cards.entity_name: Clarke Memorial Fountain and Fieldhouse Mall
cards.title: Walk through Fieldhouse Mall
cards.subtitle: Clarke Memorial Fountain and Fieldhouse Mall · Saturday afternoon
cards.notes: Use the fountain as a map-checkpoint on a walking loop, then continue through the mall toward another listed campus destination without stepping into event setups.
cards.short_summary: A named outdoor landmark on the official campus map.
cards.evidence_claim: Notre Dame’s official campus map lists Clarke Memorial Fountain and Fieldhouse Mall as a campus destination.
cards.source_title: Campus Map | University of Notre Dame
cards.access_notes: Outdoor access can be affected by weather, maintenance, or event operations.

cards.title: Check the arts calendar
cards.subtitle: DeBartolo Performing Arts Center · Saturday night
cards.notes: Choose an age-appropriate film, concert, theater, or dance event from the current calendar, and arrive early enough to clear ticketing and venue entry.
cards.short_summary: A campus venue for recurring cinematic and performing-arts programming.
cards.evidence_claim: The DeBartolo Performing Arts Center presents cinematic and performing-arts programs and lists current upcoming events.
cards.source_title: Arts & Film at Notre Dame | DeBartolo Performing Arts Center
cards.access_notes: Event availability, age guidance, and ticket requirements vary; lobby doors generally open at least one hour before events.

cards.title: Close with a campus event check
cards.subtitle: Duncan Student Center · Sunday planning stop
cards.notes: Stop in to review student-organization or campus-event information and make a simple plan for the week, keeping the first weekend’s momentum manageable.
cards.short_summary: A Student Activities-managed building designed for gathering, food, meetings, performance, and study.
cards.evidence_claim: Notre Dame’s Student Activities Office lists Duncan Student Center among the buildings it manages for gathering, eating, performing, meeting, and studying.
cards.source_title: Student Activities Office | University of Notre Dame
cards.access_notes: Consult current building and event information on site; availability may vary by scheduled programming.
